To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a picture is indeed worth one thousand words but that the words used to describe a picture can be automatically extracted from social multimedia.
a large-scale visual ontology can be built from social multimedia and that such a large-scale visual sentiment ontology enables a number of new applications in social media.
a large-scale visual ontology and classifiers can be developed from social multimedia and used to perform high-level semantic analysis and prediction of social multimedia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three aspects: (1) the design of a visual sentiment ontology, (2) the design of visual classifiers, and (3) the design of novel applications.
how to build a large-scale ontology and visual classifiers for visual sentiment and emotion detection and how to use the resulting SentiBank to develop novel applications.
how to extract the most important concepts from a large amount of data, and how to use these concepts as a basis for understanding and predicting emotions in the social multimedia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated that SentiBank is an effective system for detecting and visualizing the sentiments and emotions in visual data.
SentiBank is a powerful mid-level representation for visual content analysis.
the system we propose is the first large-scale ontology and classifier for sentiment and emotion in social multimedia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel system that combines sound structures from social multimedia and psychology to build a large-scale sentiment ontology for visual content, called SentiBank, consisting of 1200 classifiers.

we are developing the first system that automatically extracts a large-scale sentiment ontology from the folksonomy and then uses this ontology to build classifiers for detecting sentiment in visual content.

we have developed a novel large-scale visual ontology for sentiment analysis, a large-scale set of classifiers for detecting the visual concepts in SentiBank, a live sentiment prediction system and visualization tools.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the folksonomy is a rich resource for the development of a large-scale ontology and visual classifiers.
the folksonomy can be used to build large-scale visual classifiers which can be applied to a wide range of applications.

the large-scale ontology can be built from a combination of sound structures from psychology, folksonomy, and visual classifiers and that the resulting system can be applied to a variety of tasks including live social media analysis and visualization of large-scale visual data.
